subject: Greenline MAP: evaluation -> private-offer commitment & invoice flow
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@greenlinebio.com>, Greenline Procurement <procurement@greenlinebio.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Greenline MAP: evaluation -> private-offer commitment & invoice flow

Sara / Procurement team —

Thanks for the thoughtful discovery last week. Per our conversation, I’ve sketched a short mutual action plan (MAP) that aligns the evaluation sprint, technical acceptance (TAC), and the private-offer billing path you requested. Key asks from your side were: SOC 2 evidence, 30-day invoice net terms via Marketplace private offer, and a staged acceptance window for the model evaluation.

Attached is a first-pass MAP spreadsheet (greenline_map_v0.1.xlsx) that breaks down deliverables by week and owner. High-level proposal:
- Week 0–2: PoC run (pilot environment + sample dataset) — Redwood infra team + Greenline SRE
- Week 2–4: Performance/accuracy acceptance gates (predefined prompt set) — joint signoff
- Week 4–6: Legal/PO issuance & AWS private-offer setup
- Week 6: Go-live + invoice start (monthly invoices to Greenline AP via AWS marketplace vendor settlement)

Questions for you:
- Can procurement confirm the finance contact and PO routing (email/address) for net-30 invoices?
- Are there any additional procurement approvals (security attestation committee, data processing annex) that will extend the timeline?

I’ve looped in Aditya for marketplace and billing mechanics. We also have SOC 2 summary attached and a draft PO template we usually circulate to speed review.

Thanks — keen to lock the MAP and firm up dates.

—
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: greenline_map_v0.1.xlsx (spreadsheet); redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Sara Patel <sara@greenlinebio.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenline Procurement <procurement@greenlinebio.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenline MAP: evaluation -> private-offer commitment & invoice flow

Thanks Nikhil — appreciate the clear MAP. Quick responses from Procurement side:

1) Finance contact for PO/invoice: Angela Morris (angela.morris@greenlinebio.com). Please cc Angela on any billing or private-offer paperwork.
2) We need net-30 invoice terms; Greenline prefers invoices to flow through the AWS private offer settlement (so we receive one consolidated invoice monthly).
3) Security: the security committee requires SOC 2 Type II summary (not full report) and completion of our vendor questionnaire. We will circulate the questionnaire today; target is to close security review in 10 business days.
4) Approvals: Legal requires a standard DPA and confirmation of data residency (AWS us-east-1).

Tentative internal timeline:
- Security questionnaire returned: by Mon Aug 10
- Legal review and DPA sign-off: by Fri Aug 14
- PO issuance / AWS private offer creation: target week of Aug 17

If you can confirm the technical acceptance criteria (sample prompt set and latency targets) we can put hard dates on the MAP.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Patel
Head of AI Platforms, Greenline Biotech
Phone: +1 (212) 555-0199
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@greenlinebio.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Greenline Procurement <procurement@greenlinebio.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Enablement <aws-marketplace-merchant@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenline MAP: evaluation -> private-offer commitment & invoice flow

Sara / team — looping in AWS Marketplace so we can confirm private-offer mechanics. A few operational notes from Redwood:

- Private-offer path we recommend: Create an AWS Marketplace Private Offer (PO) with invoice settlement to Greenline AP. AWS will generate the purchase order link (DocuSign/accept flow) and handle invoice distribution to your AP contact.
- Documents we typically supply to speed underwriting: 1) Draft PO template (attached), 2) SOC 2 summary (attached by Nikhil), 3) Proof of vendor billing account (we can provide our marketplace seller ID).
- Technical acceptance checklist (suggested):
  * Accuracy on mapped prompt set: >= 92% pass rate across acceptance prompts (we can refine pass criteria)
  * Latency: p50 < 200ms for short prompts; p95 < 800ms (in pilot environment configured to mirror production).
  * Availability: service reachable with retry logic and KV cache priming documented.

Proposed close timeline once security/legal signoff is done:
- Day 0 (PO issued): AWS creates private-offer link -> Greenline accepts the offer in console -> Redwood receives signed commitment
- Day 7: Redwood scheduling for reserved capacity (if required) / finalize deploy artifact
- Day 14: Go-live in tenant and first invoice issued (monthly cadence thereafter)

@AWS Marketplace Enablement — can you confirm typical time-to-activate once the private offer is accepted and whether Greenline will see a single consolidated monthly invoice? Also any vendor onboarding docs we should attach to the MAP?

Thanks — Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: AWS Marketplace Enablement <aws-marketplace-merchant@amazon.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara@greenlinebio.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenline MAP: evaluation -> private-offer commitment & invoice flow

Hi all —

Confirming the Marketplace mechanics for private offers:
- Typical activation: once a Private Offer is created by the seller and accepted by the customer in the buyer console, seller entitlement is active within 24–48 hours for standard SaaS/subscription entitlements. If additional billing setup is required (invoice-only settlement), allow up to 5 business days for billing ops to finalize the invoicing config.
- Consolidated invoice: yes, Greenline will receive consolidated monthly invoices through AWS if invoice settlement is requested and approved by AWS billing. Please ensure @Angela Morris is listed as the finance contact on the offer.
- Required attachments for our underwriting: signed W-9 / tax form (US sellers), seller account id, and the draft PO/contract.

We’ve uploaded a vendor onboarding checklist here: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/vendor-onboarding (public doc) and can share a DocuSign workflow link once the draft PO is in place.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Enablement
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@greenlinebio.com>, Angela Morris <angela.morris@greenlinebio.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenline Procurement <procurement@greenlinebio.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenline MAP: evaluation -> private-offer commitment & invoice flow

Thanks everyone — small operational follow-up and final MAP attachment.

On the MAP spreadsheet I’ve added owners for each gate, an acceptance checklist template for the prompt set, and a one-page billing runbook that maps the AWS private-offer events to Redwood's invoicing and support SLA triggers. Key milestones (updated):
- Aug 10: Security questionnaire returned (Greenline)
- Aug 14: Legal/DPA sign-off
- Aug 17: Redwood submits draft PO to AWS for private-offer creation
- Aug 19–21: AWS underwriting / billing config
- Aug 24: Customer accepts private offer -> Redwood finalizes environment
- Aug 31: Go-live and first invoice cycle

Attachments: greenline_map_v0.2.xlsx (MAP with owners), greenline-draft-po-template.docx (draft PO). I also included a link to our SOC 2 summary in case procurement needs direct access (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf).

Please reply with any date conflicts; otherwise we’ll treat Aug 10 as the critical path blocker and move forward.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
